title: ALMA Subparsec Resolution Dense Molecular Line Observations of the NGC 1068 Nucleus
question: What are the dense-gas morphology, kinematics (apparent counter-rotation) and excitation of the NGC 1068 torus at sub-pc resolution in HCN and HCO+ J=4-3, and does a physically counter-rotating torus model reproduce them?

data.angular_resolution: ~350 GHz continuum and J=4-3 lines: 0.014 x 0.013 arcsec (~1 pc); reanalysed ~260 GHz: 0.019 x 0.017 arcsec (continuum), 0.020 x 0.018 (J=3-2 lines)
data.sensitivity: rms ~0.3 mJy/beam per 10 km/s channel for HCN and HCO+ J=4-3; ~0.2 mJy/beam for J=3-2

what.value: 22 GHz H2O maser spot velocities and positions (VLBI), most redshifted at V ~ 1470 km/s ~0.5 pc NW of the SMBH

evidence.quote: The most redshifted H$_{2}$O maser emission has an intensity-weighted velocity of V $\sim$ 1470 km s$^{-1}$

what.value: Best-fit analytical collision-induced counter-rotating torus model used for the position-velocity and spectra comparison

evidence.quote: Figure [10](#fig:VollmerPV) shows a detailed comparison of the position-velocity diagrams of the HCN J=4–3 and HCO$^{+}$ J=4–3 lines between our new $\lesssim$1 pc resolution data and the best-fit model of (cite: vol22).

what.value: Integrated torus fluxes HCN J=4-3 5.3 Jy km/s and HCO+ J=4-3 3.0 Jy km/s (their Table 4), compared with the new 6.8 pc aperture fluxes

evidence.quote: This recovers $\gtrsim$80% of the integrated HCN J=4–3 flux from the torus (5.3 Jy km s$^{-1}$) reported in Table 4 of (cite: vol22).

what.value: SMBH mass M_SMBH ~ 1e7 Msun, used for Keplerian velocity estimates

evidence.quote: M$_{\rm SMBH}$ $\sim$ 1 $\times$ 10$^{7}$M$_{\odot}$ (cite: gre96; hur02; lod03; gal23; gal24)

what.value: Critical densities and upper energy levels of HCN and HCO+ transitions

evidence.quote: are n$_{\rm crit}$ $\gtrsim$ 10$^{6}$ cm$^{-3}$ at a gas kinetic temperature of 50–100 K (cite: shi15)

what.value: Luminosity-to-dense-H2-mass conversion factors: 6-12 for HCN J=1-0 and 2-5 for HCO+ J=1-0 (Msun per K km/s pc2)

evidence.quote: M$_{\rm dense-H_2}$(HCN) = 6–12 $\times$ L(HCN J=1–0)

recipe.goal: Calibrate and image the Cycle 9 and Cycle 6 data
recipe.method: Start from pipeline-calibrated data, subtract continuum with uvcontsub, then tclean line and continuum cubes on a common 1.5 mas, 10 km/s grid

recipe.goal: Measure continuum and line moment-0 peaks
recipe.method: Continuum peak and integrated-intensity (moment 0) peaks of HCN, HCO+, CS at W-torus, E-torus and absorption peak, taking the highest-flux 1.5 mas pixel
assumptions: Continuum peak (C-peak) regarded as the position of the mass-accreting SMBH

recipe.method: Beam-sized spectra at C-peak, W-peak, E-peak; circular-aperture spectra of 1.7 pc diameter around W-peak and E-peak, and 3.4 and 6.8 pc diameter around C-peak

recipe.goal: Fit Gaussians to emission lines to get fluxes
recipe.method: Gaussian fits to HCN and HCO+ emission lines in area-integrated spectra (Appendix B) giving velocity-integrated fluxes

recipe.goal: Map kinematics: moment 1, moment 2, PV diagrams, compare with H2O masers
recipe.method: Intensity-weighted mean velocity (moment 1) and velocity dispersion (moment 2) maps, PV diagrams along PA = 114 deg, and comparison of the HCN J=4-3 velocity profile with VLBI H2O maser spots after a ~9 mas positional shift
key_parameters: Systemic velocity V_sys = 1130 km/s; moment-1 redshift/blueshift ranges V_sys ± 110 km/s (J=4-3) and ± 60 km/s (J=3-2) for Figures 5e,f

recipe.goal: Derive J=4-3 / J=3-2 and HCN/HCO+ flux-ratio maps
recipe.method: Ratio maps in Jy beam-1 km s-1 after matching synthesized beams, compared with 16/9 expected for thermalised optically thick emission
assumptions: Absolute flux calibration uncertainty <~10% per observation gives a maximum ratio ~2.2 for thermalised, optically thick emission

recipe.method: L' (K km/s pc2) = 3.25e7 nu_rest^-2 (1+z)^-1 D_L^2 S dV applied to the Gaussian-fit fluxes

recipe.goal: Compare data with the counter-rotating torus model
recipe.method: Compare PV diagrams and spectra along the major axis (PA = 110 deg) with the best-fit model of Vollmer et al. (2022)

recipe.goal: Estimate dense H2 gas mass in the torus
recipe.method: Assume HCN (HCO+) J=1-0 luminosity equals the J=4-3 / J=3-2 luminosity (~20e4 and ~12e4 K km/s pc2 for the 6.8 pc aperture) and apply the literature conversion factors
assumptions: Optically thick, thermalised emission; standard HCN and HCO+ abundances

recipe.goal: Test the ~400 km/s redshifted HCO+ absorption scenarios with RADEX
recipe.method: RADEX models of a foreground absorbing cloud; compare HCO+ J=4-3 vs HCN J=3-2 absorption optical depth for background temperatures of ~3 K and ~350 K
key_parameters: Volume density 1e5-1e6 cm-3, Tkin 50-150 K, N = 3e15 cm-2 for HCO+ and HCN, line width 300 km/s
assumptions: Background temperature ~350 K from the continuum brightness temperature

score_reason: Projects and key tclean parameters (robust 0.5, 1.5 mas pixel, 10 km/s) and the luminosity equation are given, but masking, line-free channels, fit details and the comparison model are not; many numeric results are tabulated.
rediscovery_reason: Both projects are cited by code and the recipe is mostly stated with tabulated numeric fluxes, luminosities and masses, though public status is not stated by the paper and cleaning details are missing.
